note: Derived from the installed 0.2.1-rc.2 packages and, for 0.2.0-rc.2, from registry tarballs verified against their published sha512 integrity hashes. The comparison is between two real package trees, not between version strings.

0.2.0-rc.2.workingDirectoryService: ABSENT — no dsh-working-directory package exists at this version
0.2.0-rc.2.workingDirectoryTool: ABSENT — no dsh-tool-working-directory package exists at this version

0.2.1-rc.2.headerCwdMutable: the header is immutable; the EFFECTIVE directory is a mutable session projection
0.2.1-rc.2.workingDirectoryService: dsh-working-directory: mutates a session projection via working-directory/change events, injects a notice, and restores the original when the current directory disappears
0.2.1-rc.2.workingDirectoryTool: dsh-tool-working-directory: model-callable `working_directory { cd?: string }` returning the absolute cwd
0.2.1-rc.2.otherConsumers: dsh-tool-bash, dsh-tool-bash-persistent, dsh-tool-fs-search, dsh-subagent, dsh-workflow-ptc, dsh-agent-instructions, dsh-tools (run_code transport)

findings.statement: the installed fs tools resolve model paths through ctx.workingDirectory.ensure(agent), not a fixed header
the installed search tools resolve their walk root through the same service
the installed release ships a mutable per-Session working-directory service
the installed release ships a model-callable `working_directory` tool with an optional absolute or relative `cd`
the committed guard resolves model paths against a FIXED cwd (config.cwd or the worker world)
the committed guard never consults the Session's effective working directory
findings.detail: no reference to workingDirectory appears in the guard

findings.statement: the executor's basis is mutable while the guard's is fixed, so the two can resolve the same model path to different objects
findings.detail: SOURCE-DEMONSTRATED HAZARD: `working_directory {cd: <dir>}` changes what every LATER tool call resolves, while the guard keeps resolving against the world

findings.statement: `subagent` takes a model-supplied `cwd` and applies it to the CHILD session, so the child's basis can move too
findings.detail: dsh-tool-subagent declares `cwd`; dsh-subagent calls workingDirectory.set(child, create.cwd)

findings.statement: `workflow` children inherit the parent's effective directory rather than choosing one
findings.detail: dsh-workflow-ptc resolves this.cwd from the PARENT session

findings.statement: removing the model-facing tool would NOT restore the equality, because delegation can still move a child's basis
findings.detail: a child created with `subagent {cwd: <protected>}` resolves relative paths against that directory while a world-fixed guard still approves them

findings.statement: 0.2.0-rc.2 resolves model paths from the immutable Session Header cwd
0.2.0-rc.2 ships no working-directory service or tool at all
findings.detail: no dsh-working-directory / dsh-tool-working-directory package exists at 0.2.0-rc.2

findings.statement: the read-boundary contract names the release it was qualified against, and drift is reported

conclusion: The guard's basis and the executor's basis are different values with different mutability. Restoring the invariant requires the guard to resolve against the SAME value the executor uses; removing the model-facing tool alone is insufficient while delegation can move a child's basis.
